problems.reason: Only mag-phase@4 needs frequency-response, yet linear-phase, decibel scale, ideal-filters and moving-average all need mag-phase@3, so it can be taught with no frequency response; make it magnitude-and-phase-response@3 needs frequency-response@3.
Sinc as the transform pair of a rect and the ideal-LPF impulse response comes from the CTFT. Sinc@3 should need continuous-time-fourier-transform@3, not the other way, and not only trig identities.

All of FIR filters' prerequisites are at @4, but fir-vs-iir-selection needs fir-filters@3, which leaves FIR@3 with none; its transfer-function, impulse-response and linear-phase arrows should start at fir-filters@3.

Windowing's prerequisites (ideal filters, FIR filters, convolution theorem, Gibbs) are only at @4, but window-function-selection needs windowing-method@3; the ideal-filter and FIR arrows should apply at windowing-method@3.
Filter specifications' prerequisites are only at @4, but window-function-selection needs filter-specifications@3; the ideal-filters and decibel-scale arrows should apply at filter-specifications@3.
iir-filters needs causality-stability-from-z-roc@3, but its ROC and LTI-property arrows apply only at @4; they should apply at @3 (ROC@3, lti-properties-from-impulse-response@3).
Aliasing, reconstruction and frequency mapping need Nyquist@3, which assumes the spectral-copy picture; nyquist-sampling-theorem@3 (not only @4) should need impulse-train-sampling@3.
anti-aliasing-filter needs aliasing@3, but aliasing has prerequisites only at @4; the Nyquist arrow should apply at aliasing@3.
The sinc concept is defined as the CTFT pair of a rect pulse, so sinc-function@3 should need continuous-time-fourier-transform@3.
The map has the CT Fourier series but no discrete-time Fourier series (DTFS), which the syllabus's Fourier-series week and the learner's discrete-time emphasis call for.
Signal energy and power has no arrow to any signal concept; it should need discrete-time-signals and continuous-time-signals.
Deciding from h whether a system is memoryless needs the memory property, so lti-properties-from-impulse-response@3 should need system-memory@2.
Linear phase as a pure delay comes from the DTFT time-shift property; linear-phase-and-group-delay@3 should need dtft-properties@3.
The syllabus only requires Calculus II, which doesn't usually cover differential equations, so constant-coefficient ODEs should be taught (briefly), not assumed as background.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.description: Numbers of the form a+jb, with their arithmetic, conjugates, magnitude, and plotting in the complex plane.

concepts.name: Euler's formula and polar form
concepts.description: The identity e^{jθ}=cosθ+j sinθ and its use to write complex numbers in magnitude-phase (polar) form.

concepts.name: Trigonometric identities
concepts.description: Standard identities for sums, products, and angle shifts of sines and cosines.

concepts.name: Integration techniques
concepts.description: Evaluating definite integrals, including substitution and integration by parts, as taught in Calculus II.

concepts.name: Improper integrals
concepts.description: Integrals over infinite limits and the conditions under which they converge.

concepts.name: Summation notation
concepts.description: Writing and manipulating finite and infinite sums with sigma notation, including index shifts.

concepts.name: Geometric series
concepts.description: Closed-form sums of finite and infinite geometric series and the condition |r|<1 for convergence.

concepts.name: Partial fraction decomposition
concepts.description: Splitting a rational function into a sum of simpler fractions with first- or second-order denominators.

concepts.name: Linear constant-coefficient differential equations
concepts.description: Ordinary differential equations with constant coefficients that describe continuous-time systems.

concepts.name: Continuous-time signals
concepts.description: Functions x(t) defined for every real value of time, used to model physical quantities.

concepts.name: Discrete-time signals
concepts.description: Sequences x[n] defined only at integer indices, such as sampled data.

concepts.name: Time shifting, scaling, and reversal
concepts.description: Transforming a signal's independent variable by shifting, time-reversing, or scaling it, including the order in which to apply these operations.

concepts.name: Even and odd decomposition
concepts.description: Writing any signal as the sum of an even part (x(t)+x(-t))/2 and an odd part (x(t)-x(-t))/2.

concepts.name: Signal periodicity
concepts.description: Whether a continuous- or discrete-time signal repeats, and finding its fundamental period, including the integer-period condition for discrete sinusoids.

concepts.name: Signal energy and power
concepts.description: Total energy and average power of a signal, computed by integrating or summing its squared magnitude.

concepts.name: Discrete-time unit impulse and unit step
concepts.description: The sequences δ[n] and u[n], how they relate, and how any sequence can be written as a sum of shifted impulses.

concepts.name: Dirac delta function
concepts.description: The continuous-time unit impulse δ(t), defined by its sifting property under integration.

concepts.name: Complex exponential and sinusoidal signals
concepts.description: Signals of the form e^{st} or z^n and the real sinusoids built from them, in continuous and discrete time.

concepts.name: Linearity
concepts.description: The system property that the response to a weighted sum of inputs equals the same weighted sum of the individual responses.

concepts.name: Time invariance
concepts.description: The system property that shifting the input in time shifts the output by the same amount and changes nothing else.

concepts.name: Causality
concepts.description: The system property that the output at any time depends only on present and past inputs.

concepts.name: BIBO stability
concepts.description: The system property that every bounded input produces a bounded output.

concepts.name: System memory
concepts.description: Whether a system's output depends only on the current input (memoryless) or also on other times (with memory).

concepts.name: Linear time-invariant (LTI) systems
concepts.description: Systems that are both linear and time-invariant, so that their impulse response fully describes them.

concepts.name: Impulse response
concepts.description: The output h of an LTI system when the input is a unit impulse. It fully determines how the system responds to any input.

concepts.name: Discrete-time convolution
concepts.description: Computing an LTI system's output with the convolution sum y[n]=Σ x[k]h[n−k].

concepts.name: Continuous-time convolution
concepts.description: Computing an LTI system's output with the convolution integral y(t)=∫x(τ)h(t−τ)dτ, using the flip-and-slide method.

concepts.name: Properties of convolution
concepts.description: The commutative, associative, and distributive properties of convolution and what they mean for systems in series and in parallel.

concepts.name: LTI system properties from the impulse response
concepts.description: Deciding whether an LTI system is causal, stable, or memoryless by examining its impulse response, for example by checking absolute summability for stability.

concepts.name: Complex exponentials as eigenfunctions of LTI systems
concepts.description: The fact that a complex exponential input to an LTI system produces the same exponential at the output, scaled by a complex gain.

concepts.name: Continuous-time Fourier series
concepts.description: Writing a periodic signal as a weighted sum of harmonically related complex exponentials, and computing the coefficients.

concepts.name: Gibbs phenomenon
concepts.description: The overshoot and ripple that stay near a jump discontinuity when a Fourier representation is truncated.

concepts.name: Parseval's theorem
concepts.description: The equality between a signal's energy or power in the time domain and in the frequency domain.

concepts.name: Continuous-time Fourier transform
concepts.description: The transform X(jω)=∫x(t)e^{−jωt}dt and its inverse, which represent aperiodic continuous-time signals in frequency.

concepts.name: Sinc function
concepts.description: The function sin(πx)/(πx), which is the Fourier pair of a rectangular pulse and the impulse response of an ideal lowpass filter.

concepts.name: Fourier transform properties
concepts.description: Properties such as linearity, time shift, frequency shift (modulation), scaling, duality, and differentiation, used to compute transforms without integrating.

concepts.name: Convolution theorem
concepts.description: Convolution in time corresponds to multiplication in frequency, and multiplication in time corresponds to convolution in frequency.

concepts.name: Discrete-time Fourier transform (DTFT)
concepts.description: The transform X(e^{jω})=Σx[n]e^{−jωn}, which is 2π-periodic and represents discrete-time signals in frequency.

concepts.name: DTFT properties
concepts.description: Properties of the DTFT such as linearity, time shift, modulation, and 2π-periodicity, used to compute transforms of sequences.

concepts.name: Frequency response
concepts.description: The function H(e^{jω}) or H(jω) that gives an LTI system's complex gain at each frequency, equal to the Fourier transform of its impulse response.

concepts.name: Magnitude and phase response
concepts.description: Splitting a frequency response into |H| (gain) and ∠H (phase shift), then computing and plotting each against frequency.

concepts.name: Linear phase and group delay
concepts.description: A phase response that is linear in frequency delays every frequency component by the same amount, and group delay measures that delay.

concepts.name: Decibel magnitude scale
concepts.description: Expressing gain as 20·log10|H| in decibels to read attenuation and ripple on frequency-response plots.

concepts.name: Impulse-train sampling model
concepts.description: Modeling sampling as multiplication by a periodic impulse train, which makes copies of the spectrum at multiples of the sampling frequency.

concepts.name: Nyquist sampling theorem
concepts.description: A bandlimited signal can be recovered exactly from its samples if the sampling rate is greater than twice its highest frequency.

concepts.name: Aliasing
concepts.description: When a signal is sampled too slowly, its spectral copies overlap and high frequencies show up as false low frequencies.

concepts.name: Reconstruction from samples
concepts.description: Recovering a continuous-time signal from its samples by ideal lowpass filtering, which is the same as sinc interpolation.

concepts.name: Continuous-to-discrete frequency mapping
concepts.description: The relation ω=ΩT between analog frequency in rad/s or Hz and digital frequency in radians per sample, used to convert specifications.

concepts.name: Anti-aliasing filter
concepts.description: An analog lowpass filter applied before sampling to remove frequencies above half the sampling rate.

concepts.name: Laplace transform
concepts.description: The transform X(s)=∫x(t)e^{−st}dt, which extends the Fourier transform to complex frequencies s=σ+jω.

concepts.name: Laplace region of convergence
concepts.description: The set of s-values where the Laplace integral converges, and what it says about whether a signal is right-sided, left-sided, causal, or stable.

concepts.name: Poles and zeros in the s-plane
concepts.description: The roots of the denominator and numerator of a rational Laplace transform, plotted in the s-plane, and how their locations relate to time-domain behavior.

concepts.name: Inverse Laplace transform
concepts.description: Recovering a time signal from a rational X(s) and its ROC, using partial fractions and known transform pairs.

concepts.name: Continuous-time transfer function
concepts.description: The system function H(s), the Laplace transform of the impulse response, found from a system's differential equation.

concepts.name: Z-transform
concepts.description: The transform X(z)=Σx[n]z^{−n}, which generalizes the DTFT to complex values of z.

concepts.name: Z-transform region of convergence
concepts.description: The ring of z-values where the z-transform sum converges, and how its shape shows whether a sequence is right-sided, left-sided, or two-sided.

concepts.name: Z-transform properties
concepts.description: Properties such as linearity, time shift (multiplying by z^{−k}), convolution, and scaling, used to manipulate z-transforms.

concepts.name: Inverse z-transform
concepts.description: Recovering a sequence from a rational X(z) and its ROC, using partial fractions, standard pairs, or power-series expansion.

concepts.name: Poles and zeros in the z-plane
concepts.description: The roots of the numerator and denominator of a rational H(z), plotted relative to the unit circle.

concepts.name: Causality and stability from the z-domain
concepts.description: A causal LTI system is stable exactly when all its poles lie inside the unit circle, which means its ROC includes the unit circle.

concepts.name: Relationship between the z-transform and the DTFT
concepts.description: The DTFT equals the z-transform evaluated on the unit circle z=e^{jω}, provided the ROC contains the unit circle.

concepts.name: Geometric evaluation of frequency response from pole-zero plots
concepts.description: Estimating magnitude and phase response from the distances and angles between a point on the unit circle and the system's poles and zeros.

concepts.name: Linear constant-coefficient difference equations
concepts.description: Equations that relate current and past outputs to current and past inputs, used to describe and compute discrete-time LTI systems recursively.

concepts.name: Discrete-time transfer function
concepts.description: The rational system function H(z)=Y(z)/X(z), found from a difference equation or an impulse response.

concepts.name: System block diagrams and realizations
concepts.description: Building a difference equation or transfer function from adders, multipliers, and delays, for example in Direct Form I or II.

concepts.name: Ideal frequency-selective filters
concepts.description: Ideal lowpass, highpass, and bandpass filters with brick-wall magnitude responses, and why their infinite, noncausal impulse responses can't be built.

concepts.name: Filter specifications
concepts.description: Describing a practical filter by its passband and stopband edges, transition width, passband ripple, and stopband attenuation.

concepts.name: FIR filters
concepts.description: Finite impulse response filters, which are nonrecursive, always stable, and can have exactly linear phase.

concepts.name: IIR filters
concepts.description: Infinite impulse response filters, which use feedback (poles) to get sharp responses with few coefficients but can be unstable and have nonlinear phase.

concepts.name: Moving-average filter
concepts.description: The FIR lowpass filter that averages the last M samples, and its sinc-like (Dirichlet) magnitude response.

concepts.name: Choosing between FIR and IIR
concepts.description: Choosing an FIR or IIR filter by weighing phase linearity, guaranteed stability, filter order, and computational cost against the specification.

concepts.name: Windowing method for FIR design
concepts.description: Designing an FIR filter by truncating and delaying the ideal filter's sinc impulse response and multiplying it by a finite window.

concepts.name: Window function selection
concepts.description: Choosing among rectangular, Hann, Hamming, and similar windows, and choosing the window length, by trading main-lobe width (transition width) against side-lobe level (stopband attenuation).

concepts.name: Filter design by pole-zero placement
concepts.description: Designing a simple IIR or FIR filter by placing poles near the passband and zeros in the stopband, for example a first-order recursive lowpass filter.

concepts.name: Digital lowpass filter design and analysis
concepts.description: The full process of turning lowpass specifications into a working digital filter: picking FIR or IIR, finding the coefficients, and checking the frequency response, stability, and realization.
